duration.$description: Only for motion a user cannot interrupt (hover, colour, opacity, small state changes). Anything the user can grab or reverse uses a spring. UI motion stays under 300 ms; exits are shorter than entries. Actions triggered from the keyboard do not animate.

instant.$description: Press feedback. Shown on pointer-down, never on release.

deliberate.$description: Signature moments only: the logo drawing in, first run.

out.$description: Default. Anything entering, leaving or responding to the user. Exits use the same curve, only shorter.

in-out.$description: Things that travel from one place to another while staying on screen.

sheet.$description: Sheets and drawers when a spring is not available.

standard.$description: Colour, opacity and other non-spatial changes.

spring.$description: Apple-style parameters: response in seconds (how fast it reaches the target) and damping ratio (1 = no overshoot). The build also emits a CSS linear() curve and a settle duration for each, for places where a spring library is not available. In code prefer a real, interruptible spring with the same parameters.

default.$description: Critically damped. The house default for anything that moves.

snappy.$description: Small controls: toggles, segmented controls, checkmarks.

gentle.$description: Large surfaces: panels, sheets, layout shifts.

momentum.$description: A little overshoot. Only where the gesture itself carried momentum: a flicked sheet, a dropped item, a thrown card.

spinner-period.$description: One turn of the in-progress arc. Linear.

pulse-period.$description: Breathing of a live model while it generates. Opacity only, never scale.

stagger.$description: Delay between list items entering. Cap the total at 240 ms.
